class S2D4P.loss.kld.BetaAnnealing(beta: float = 1, beta_min: float = 0, num_epoch_to_warmup: int = 0, num_epochs_to_hold: int = 0)

Bases: object

Configure annealing of the Kullback-Leibler divergence weight.

The beta coefficient increases linearly from beta_min to beta over the configured warmup period. An optional hold period produces a repeating cyclical schedule.

Parameters:

  • beta (float) – Maximum KLD weight reached after warmup.

  • beta_min (float) – Minimum KLD weight at the beginning of each warmup period.

  • num_epoch_to_warmup (int) – Number of epochs over which beta increases from beta_min to beta.

  • num_epochs_to_hold (int) – Number of additional epochs included in each annealing cycle after beta reaches its maximum value.

beta: float = 1
beta_min: float = 0
build(num_batches)

Initialize the beta schedule from the number of batches per epoch.

The configured warmup and hold periods are converted from epochs to training steps.

Parameters:

num_batches (int) – Number of training batches in each epoch.

num_epoch_to_warmup: int = 0
num_epochs_to_hold: int = 0
class S2D4P.loss.kld.KLD(reduction: Literal['mean', 'sum'] = 'mean')

Bases: lossABC

Compute Kullback-Leibler divergence for a variational latent distribution.

Supports divergence relative to a standard normal prior, a condition-dependent Gaussian prior, or a learned normalizing-flow prior.

Parameters:

reduction (Reduction) – Reduction applied to the KLD across latent dimensions and samples.

forward(mu: Tensor, log_var: Tensor, cond_mu: Tensor | None = None, cond_log_var: Tensor | None = None, prior_flow: NormalizedFlowModel | None = None, print_loss=False) → Tensor

Compute the Kullback-Leibler divergence.

Without a normalizing flow, the posterior Gaussian is compared analytically with either a condition-dependent Gaussian prior or a standard normal prior. With a normalizing flow, the divergence is estimated from posterior samples using posterior and transformed-prior log probabilities together with the flow log-determinant.

Parameters:

  • mu (torch.Tensor) – Mean of the posterior latent distribution.

  • log_var (torch.Tensor) – Log-variance of the posterior latent distribution.

  • cond_mu (torch.Tensor | None) – Mean of the condition-dependent Gaussian prior.

  • cond_log_var (torch.Tensor | None) – Log-variance of the condition-dependent Gaussian prior.

  • prior_flow (NormalizedFlowModel | None) – Optional normalizing flow defining the latent prior.

  • print_loss (bool) – Whether to print the calculated KLD value.

Returns:

Reduced Kullback-Leibler divergence.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

AssertionError – If posterior mean and log-variance shapes differ, or if both conditional prior parameters are provided with incompatible shapes.

class S2D4P.loss.loss.Losspipeline(config: LosspipelineConfig, weights: DataArray, num_output_dimensions: int = 2, generative_context: GenerativeContext | None = None)

Bases: Module

Combine multiple weighted loss functions into one training objective.

Each configured loss term is constructed from the loss registry with shared reduction, spatial and variable weights, output dimensionality, and generative context. Optional target masks and a fixed output mask can be applied before individual losses are evaluated.

Parameters:

  • config (LosspipelineConfig) – Configuration defining loss terms, weights, masking, and reduction.

  • weights (xr.DataArray) – Spatial and variable weights supplied to each loss term.

  • num_output_dimensions (int) – Number of model output dimensions expected by each loss function.

  • generative_context (GenerativeContext | None) – Context describing generative-model and generator behavior.

forward(data, target, target_mask=None, print_loss=False, step_arguments: dict | None = None)

Evaluate and combine all configured loss terms.

An optional fixed output mask is combined with the target mask before loss calculation. Each loss term is evaluated independently and multiplied by its configured weight before contributing to the total loss.

Parameters:

  • data (torch.Tensor) – Model predictions supplied to each loss function.

  • target (torch.Tensor) – Target values used to calculate the losses.

  • target_mask (torch.Tensor | None) – Optional validity mask applied during loss calculation.

  • print_loss (bool) – Whether individual loss functions print their calculated values.

  • step_arguments (dict | None) – Additional keyword arguments passed to each loss function.

Returns:

Weighted total loss and detached individual loss values keyed by loss step name.

Return type:

tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]

Raises:

AssertionError – If the target dimensionality is incompatible with the configured number of output dimensions and generative-model context.

Parameters:

  • loss_weights (list of float or None, optional) – Weights applied to each loss term.

  • reduction ({"mean", "sum"}, optional) – Reduction method applied to individual losses.

  • saved_output_mask_dir (str or None) –

    Location of a saved fixed output maks for loss calculation. The mask could have any of the following shapes:

    1- C, D1, D2, .. 2- 1, D1, D2, … 3- D1, D2, …

    where C is channel size and D1, D2, … are output sizes. The sizes must match that of the input and target data.

class S2D4P.loss.registery.Registery

Bases: object

Registry for named classes.

Registered classes can be retrieved and instantiated by name using optional configuration data.

available()

Return the names of all registered classes.

Returns:

Names currently available in the registry.

Return type:

list[str]

get(name, config=None)

Retrieve and instantiate a registered class.

Dictionary configurations are expanded into constructor arguments. Dataclass types are constructed using strict field matching, while other dictionary configurations are passed as keyword arguments. Non-dictionary configuration values are passed as a single positional argument.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – Name identifying the registered class.

  • config (Any) – Configuration used to construct the registered class.

Returns:

Instance of the registered class.

Any

S2D4P.loss.utils_loss module

class S2D4P.loss.utils_loss.Frobenius_norm(weights: DataArray, reduction: Literal['mean', 'sum'] = 'mean', num_output_dimensions: int = 2, generative_context: GenerativeContext | None = None, covariance_dim: Literal['spatial', 'channel'] = 'spatial')

Bases: lossABC

Measure covariance mismatch using the Frobenius norm.

Covariance matrices are calculated from targets and predictions either across spatial features within each channel or across channels. Their difference is measured with the matrix Frobenius norm.

Parameters:

  • weights (xr.DataArray) – Target weight array used to determine the spatial output size.

  • reduction (Reduction) – Reduction applied to the covariance discrepancy.

  • num_output_dimensions (int) – Number of model output dimensions, including the channel dimension.

  • generative_context (GenerativeContext | None) – Context describing generative-model and generator behavior.

  • covariance_dim (CovarianceDim) – Dimension over which covariance structure is compared. Supported values are "spatial" and "channel".

forward(data: Tensor, target: Tensor, target_mask: Tensor | None = None, print_loss: bool = False) → Tensor

Compute covariance discrepancy between predictions and targets.

Generator outputs are first averaged across their output-sample dimension. Spatial dimensions are flattened before covariance matrices are calculated across spatial features or channels.

Parameters:

  • data (torch.Tensor) – Model predictions.

  • target (torch.Tensor) – Target values.

  • target_mask (torch.Tensor | None) – Optional target mask. This loss does not currently use the mask.

  • print_loss (bool) – Whether to print the calculated loss.

Returns:

Reduced Frobenius norm of the prediction and target covariance difference.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

AssertionError – If prediction and target shapes do not match after generator samples are resolved.

class S2D4P.loss.utils_loss.WeightedCRPS(weights: DataArray, reduction: Literal['mean', 'sum'] = 'mean', num_output_dimensions: int = 2, low_ress_kernel_size: int | None = None, generative_context: GenerativeContext | None = None, **kwargs)

Bases: lossABC

Compute weighted continuous ranked probability score.

CRPS is evaluated from an ensemble of generator predictions and supports spatial and variable weights, optional masking, and optional low-resolution pooling.

Parameters:

  • weights (xr.DataArray) – Spatial and optional channel weights applied to CRPS values.

  • reduction (Reduction) – Reduction applied to weighted CRPS values.

  • num_output_dimensions (int) – Number of model output dimensions, including the channel dimension.

  • low_ress_kernel_size (int | None) – Kernel size used to downsample predictions, targets, masks, and weights before calculating CRPS.

  • generative_context (GenerativeContext | None) – Context describing generative-model and generator behavior.

  • kwargs (Any) – Additional unused keyword arguments accepted for pipeline compatibility.

forward(data: Tensor, target: Tensor, target_mask: Tensor | None = None, print_loss=False) → Tensor

Compute the weighted continuous ranked probability score.

For a single ensemble member, CRPS reduces to absolute error. For multiple members, the ensemble is sorted and the empirical CRPS is calculated from its distance to the target and pairwise ensemble spacing.

Parameters:

  • data (torch.Tensor) – Ensemble predictions with a leading output-sample dimension.

  • target (torch.Tensor) – Target values.

  • target_mask (torch.Tensor | None) – Optional validity mask applied during loss aggregation.

  • print_loss (bool) – Whether to print the calculated loss.

Returns:

Reduced weighted CRPS.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

RuntimeError – If generator-based output sampling is not enabled.

class S2D4P.loss.utils_loss.WeightedMSE(weights: DataArray, reduction: Literal['mean', 'sum'] = 'mean', num_output_dimensions: int = 2, low_ress_kernel_size: int | None = None, generative_context: GenerativeContext | None = None, hyperparam=1.0, min_threshold=0, max_threshold=0, **kwargs)

Bases: lossABC

Compute weighted mean squared error.

Supports spatial and variable weights, optional masking, optional low-resolution pooling, threshold-dependent error scaling, and generator outputs. For generator models, predictions are averaged across the output-sample dimension before squared error is calculated.

Parameters:

  • weights (xr.DataArray) – Spatial and optional channel weights applied to squared errors.

  • reduction (Reduction) – Reduction applied to the weighted squared errors.

  • num_output_dimensions (int) – Number of model output dimensions, including the channel dimension.

  • low_ress_kernel_size (int | None) – Kernel size used to downsample predictions, targets, masks, and weights before calculating the loss. If None, no downsampling is applied.

  • generative_context (GenerativeContext | None) – Context describing generative-model and generator behavior.

  • hyperparam (float) – Multiplicative penalty applied to errors that cross the configured thresholds.

  • min_threshold (float) – Lower target threshold used for asymmetric error weighting.

  • max_threshold (float) – Upper target threshold used for asymmetric error weighting.

  • kwargs (Any) – Additional unused keyword arguments accepted for pipeline compatibility.

forward(data: Tensor, target: Tensor, target_mask: Tensor | None = None, print_loss=False) → Tensor

Compute weighted mean squared error.

Generator outputs are averaged across their output-sample dimension. Optional low-resolution pooling and threshold-dependent penalties are applied before the weighted loss is reduced.

Parameters:

  • data (torch.Tensor) – Model predictions.

  • target (torch.Tensor) – Target values.

  • target_mask (torch.Tensor | None) – Optional validity mask applied during loss aggregation.

  • print_loss (bool) – Whether to print the calculated loss.

Returns:

Reduced weighted mean squared error.

Return type:

torch.Tensor

Raises:

RuntimeError – If the prediction and target shapes do not match after generator samples are resolved.
